suite.doc:
FM follows the 12.5/25 kHz channel bandwidth setting, on transmit and on receive, on every band the radio has.
Run it with a bench's argument file (bench/example.args), whose oat.expand repeats each test on every band in the radio file. Transmit is measured from the SDR capture; receive is judged by the operator, until the radio can report its own audio. The programming cable stays out throughout: it disconnects the mic and the speaker.
A bench with an audio interface on the accessory jack keys the radio and plays the test tones into the mic itself; otherwise the operator plays a tone at the mic, whistles and keys.
To measure stock firmware as a reference, exclude mode:m17.

suite.doc:
FM audio, on transmit and on receive, measured electrically: test audio goes into the mic input and the speaker is recorded through a USB sound interface on the radio's accessory connector (the bench file's audio section). The connector must mute the internal mic and speaker while plugged; check that once per radio.
Every test needs the audio interface (needs:audio); the receive sensitivity also needs absolute transmitter levels (needs:abs-level). Key-ups go through the interface's PTT line when the bench has one, otherwise the operator keys on request. Run it on every firmware state to compare: stock firmware included, with -v FIRMWARE:stock-... and -v DSP:stock.
